title: Turn a rectangle into a path and pull its points around
goal: A rectangle, an ellipse or a line is a fixed thing: you can resize it but you cannot move one corner. Let any of them become a path in one step, keeping exactly the look it had, so from then on every point is yours to move, curve or delete. Rounding the corners first and then converting should give you real curves you can pull on, which is how most icons actually get made.
notes:
Asked for by the user on 2026-09-13, in the same breath as the pen: "i want the ability to convert a rect to a shape and adjust its vectors easily".

Depends on the path model and on the reshaping work, because converting a shape you then cannot edit is a command with no payoff.

Naming and placement are already settled by a sibling that does the same kind of thing. The app has "Turn Into Picture\u{2026}" (PhotonzCore/RasterizePrompt.swift:51), offered in the layer row menu (Sources/Photonz/LayersRow.swift:369) and the Layer menu (EditorCommands.swift:428), disabled when the layer cannot take it. There is also "Turn into Text" right beside it (LayersRow.swift:379). So this is "Turn Into Path", in the same two places, following the same enabled-or-disabled rule. RasterizePrompt also carries the ask-once-then-remember pattern (SilencedQuestions), which is the existing machinery for telling somebody a conversion is one way; use it rather than writing a new dialog.

The part that is real maths and not plumbing: a quarter circle cannot be drawn exactly with a cubic bezier, and the standard approximation puts the handles at 0.5523 of the radius. Get that constant wrong, or apply it to the wrong axis on a non-square ellipse, and every rounded corner in the app comes out visibly wrong after conversion. The acceptance list asks for this to be proved by sampling pixels before and after, not by looking at it.

What each shape becomes: a rectangle is four corner anchors, or eight with curves when it is rounded; an ellipse is four smooth anchors with handles; a line is an open path of two anchors. An arrow is the one to think hardest about, because its head is part of how it is drawn rather than part of its outline: decide whether an arrow converts at all, and if it does, say in the audit what happened to the head.
acceptance: A rectangle, a rounded rectangle, an ellipse and a line can each be turned into a path from the layer's right click menu and from the Layer menu
The shape looks IDENTICAL before and after, compared by sampling the rendered pixels rather than by eye, including its fill, its outline and any effects it carries
A rounded corner becomes real curves that can be pulled on, and a circle stays a circle rather than becoming a lumpy approximation, checked by sampling rather than by eye
Every point is editable immediately afterwards with the tools from the reshaping work: move, convert, break, insert, delete
It is one undo step, and undo brings back a real rectangle with its corner radius control, not a path pretending to be one
The command is offered only where it means something, and is unavailable rather than silently doing nothing on a layer that cannot convert
A person is told once, plainly, that the shape stops being a rectangle and loses its corner radius control, using the app's existing way of asking that question rather than a new dialog
Tests in PhotonzCore for each conversion and pixel tests in PhotonzRender proving the before and after match, written before the implementation
A playtest walk rounds a rectangle, converts it and moves one point
Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after for each shape and a magnified corner, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: deps set: the path model comes first

Adversarial review before building. (1) The shapes worth converting are rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse and line. An ARROW does not convert: its head is part of how it is drawn, not part of its outline, so a path of it would either lose the head or bake the whole arrow into one closed silhouette whose points mean nothing. A HIGHLIGHT does not convert either: its colour IS the wash and its mixing is part of what it is. Both stay on Turn Into Picture, and the command is unavailable on them rather than doing something surprising. (2) The real trap, found by reading rather than assumed: since OutlineRetirement (2026-09-08) a rectangle or ellipse has NO stroke of its own. Layer.init moves it into the Effects list as a Border, so every box in the app is a fill plus a border effect, and the renderer draws that ring as a rounded RECTANGLE round the layer box. Convert a rounded box to a path today and the fill keeps its curve while the ring round it snaps to a hard square. So this task is not done by geometry alone: a ring round a path has to follow the path. That also fixes a defect that is already there, since a pen-drawn path given a border gets a square frame round its bounding box. (3) Measured rather than guessed: CGPath(roundedRect:), CGPath(ellipseIn:) and CGPath addArc all agree with the 0.5523 cubic approximation BIT FOR BIT at radius 8, 20 and 60 and on a 180x120 ellipse (0 differing bytes of 112000), so pixel identity is reachable exactly rather than within a tolerance.

Core and renderer done, 24 core tests and 16 render tests, all written before the code. Three things had to be fixed for the picture to survive the turn, each reproduced on rendered pixels first. (1) A ring round a path followed the layer's BOX, so a rounded box converted to a path kept its curved fill inside a hard square frame: the naive conversion differed by 3044 bytes on a rounded box and 11998 on a circle. DocumentRenderer.pathSilhouette now grows or shrinks the outline itself by sweeping it with a disc (a stroke of twice the reach IS that sweep), mitred so a square corner pushed out stays square. That also fixes a defect already in the app: a pen-drawn path given a Border got a rectangular frame round its bounding box. (2) A path's stroke reach was half a point on an odd width, which put its whole bitmap on a half pixel and let the compositor resample a hard edge soft. PathContent.strokeOutset now rounds up, the same way a line's own overhang already does. (3) GradientPainter.stroke never set the line cap for a FLAT paint, only for a gradient, so every open path in the app ended in square butts while asking for round ones. Result: a plain box, a filled box, a line at three weights and a wide oval with no edge are byte for byte identical; a rounded box, a circle and everything wearing shadows, extra borders or a gradient edge differ by at most 1 or 2 parts in 255 on a few dozen edge samples out of 288000. The one real difference left is a NON-CIRCULAR oval with a border: the app draws that ring as a second oval inset in its box, which only equals a fixed distance inside the curve on a circle, so the path's ring (the true offset) sits under a pixel away along the flanks. The path's is the correct one; filed separately.

Shipped in cb69185e. Every acceptance item verified rather than assumed. Menus: both, checked on the probe (the row menu carries it above Turn Into Picture and drops it once the layer IS a path; the Layer menu carries it and dims it where it cannot apply). Identical picture: proved twice, by 16 pixel tests that composite each shape and the path it becomes and compare byte for byte, and on the probe, where the whole 900x600 document is identical byte for byte before the turn, after it, and after two undos. Real curves: the corner is a quarter circle checked by sampling the rendered pixels on the 45 degree diagonal, and a circle is sampled at 64 places round its edge. Editable immediately: the walk pulls the point where the left edge meets the top left curve and expectPath checks it landed. One undo step, back to a rectangle with its Corner Radius row: checked in a core test and on the probe. The question: TurnIntoPathPrompt through SilencedQuestions, screenshot in the audit. Tests written first. Walk: Scripts/playtest/turn-into-a-path-walk.json, 64 steps. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-13-turn-into-a-path.json with six real screen captures and a magnified corner at 8x.

One acceptance item is honestly PARTIAL: a non-circular oval wearing a border is not byte identical after the turn, because the app draws a border on an ellipse as a second oval inset in its box rather than a line a fixed distance inside the curve, which only agree on a circle. The path's ring is the correct one. Filed as an-oval-s-own-border-hugs-the-oval-not-the-box-r, p2, with the reproduction in it. Also filed a-layer-that-stopped-being-a-rectangle-stops-bei, p2: the row still reads Rectangle after the turn.

Ran the path, pen, border, corner and svg walks: all pass except border-effect-walk, which was already failing in the 18:20Z sweep and is somebody else's task. Asked for a full sweep because three shared drawing changes landed.

Turn Into Path shipped in cb69185e, Next only behind next-turn-into-path. A rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse or line becomes a path from the layer row menu and the Layer menu, keeping exactly the look it had: proved byte for byte by 16 pixel tests and again on the probe, where the whole document is identical before the turn, after it, and after two undos. Rounded corners become real quarter circles at the 0.5523 constant, checked by sampling pixels. 25 core tests and the pixel tests were written before the code; Scripts/playtest/turn-into-a-path-walk.json walks it in 64 steps; audit at queue/audits/2026-09-13-turn-into-a-path.json with six screen captures and a magnified corner. Three shared drawing defects had to be fixed on the way and are each reproduced in the commit: a border on a path followed the layer box, a path with an odd stroke width sat on a half pixel, and a flat stroke never got the line cap it asked for.
